first_end.mechanism: express revocation by EO 12553: its operative sentence ends with the words "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and is followed by a two-column table headed 'No. Subject' whose entry "11170 Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes" names this order by number; EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording (the full held text was searched for effective, take effect, except, provided, saving, nothing and pending), so the revocation is read as taking effect on signing, February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986; filed February 26, 1986). The signing-date reading is an inference from the order's heading and signature block, not express wording.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: The order's single operative text creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate disputes between the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and certain of their employees represented by the Five Cooperating Railway Labor Organizations, directs it to report within thirty days, and recites the statutory standstill for thirty days after the report. It ended with the whole order: first end EO 12553, 1986-02-25, which revokes the order by number ("11170 Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes"). The report deadline is a deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines), and the end of the standstill is a spent fact whose date no held reviewed source fixes, so neither is recorded as an earlier end or as a later event. The order states no end date of its own, and no held instrument other than EO 12553 names it.

TWEEN THE CARRIERS REPRESENTED BY THE NATIONAL RAILWAY
LABOR CONFERENCE AND CERTAIN OF THEIR EMPLOYEES
W HEREAS disputes exist between the carriers represented by the 
National Railway Labor Conference, designated in List A attached 
hereto and made a part thereof, and certain of their employees rep­
resented by the Five Cooperating Railway Labor Organizations, labor 
organizations, designated in List B attached hereto and made a part 
hereof; and
W HEREAS these disputes have not heretofore been adjusted under 
the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
W HEREAS these disputes, in the judgment of the National Medi­
ation Board, threaten substantially to interrupt interstate commerce 
to a degree such as to deprive the country of essential transportation 
service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
Section 10, of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 TJ.S.C. 160), 
I  hereby create a board to be appointed by me, to investigate these 
disputes. No member of the board shall be pecuniarily or otherwise 
interested in any organization of railroad employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to 
the disputes within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report 
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by 
the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference, or 
by their employees, in the conditions out of which the disputes arose.

research_rationale:
EO 11170 (1964-08-18, 29 FR 11893) creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate disputes between the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and certain of their employees represented by the Five Cooperating Railway Labor Organizations, directs the board to report within thirty days, and recites the statutory standstill that section 10 imposes on the parties from the order's date until thirty days after the report. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11170.txt, 29 FR 11893, PDF pages 13-16) and confirmed that its printed number, title and signature date match the census register row. The order has one operative paragraph with no numbered sections and no stated end date, so the dossier's single whole-order clause is the complete inventory (any carrier list the order attaches is an incorporated list, not a separate command). EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt) revokes the order by number in its table. The first end is that express revocation. The report deadline, the report itself and the end of the standstill are not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, and no held reviewed source establishes the dates on which the board reported or the standstill ran out. Bounded search read for this order: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09; eCFR and GovInfo CFR bulk through 2026-10-14; Federal Register catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts), after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning; the Cruden by-number scan of held order texts in the packet's LOOKUPS.md; and a full read of EO 12553 (held FR text, 33,227 characters).
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Own terms: the order states a report deadline (\"within thirty days from the date of this order\") and a standstill running (\"for thirty days after the board has made its report\"). A report deadline is a deadline, not an end, and the standstill is a spent fact whose date no held source fixes; neither is recorded as an end. The order states no date on which it ends. Held later instruments: the by-number scan lists no held later order that cites this order other than EO 12553, which names it in its revocation table; the Federal Register catalog note records the EO 12553 revocation and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches return no hit. No unnamed statute or order was found that would be an earlier candidate end beyond section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, the statute the order itself invokes.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order (1) creates the board and bars members with a financial or organizational interest, (2) directs a report within thirty days and (3) recites the section 10 standstill. Command (3) rests on the statute, which binds the parties for its own thirty-day period regardless of the order, so it is not an independent surviving command of the order. The order makes no appointment by name, creates no fund or property right and delegates no continuing authority, so nothing in it outlives its revocation.","savings_check":"Savings: no savings language in EO 12553 or in this order; the completed facts are spent and nothing continues independently.","scope_check":"Whole-order scope: EO 12553 revokes the order in full. Its table lists the order by number with no 'in part' or section limitation, so the single clause ends on the revocation date, and the held sources record no partial amendment of this order."}

savings_residuals.reason: EO 12553 has no savings, exception, pending-matter or 'nothing herein' wording (searched in the full held text). Its revocation therefore leaves nothing of this order in operation. The creation of the board, any report and the statutory standstill are completed facts, not continuing commands; their dates are not established by a held reviewed source, so no earlier end is claimed. The order created no continuing right, fund or appointment.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: The order's single operative text creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate disputes between the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Firemen and Enginemen, directs it to report within thirty days, and recites the statutory standstill for thirty days after the report. It ended with the whole order: first end EO 12553, 1986-02-25, which revokes the order by number ("11180 Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes"). The report deadline is a deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines), and the end of the standstill is a spent fact whose date no held reviewed source fixes, so neither is recorded as an earlier end or as a later event. The order states no end date of its own, and no held instrument other than EO 12553 names it.

Executive Order 11180
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE DISPUTES BE­
TWEEN THE CARRIERS REPRESENTED BY THE NATIONAL RAILWAY
LABOR.CONFERENCE AND CERTAIN OF THEIR EMPLOYEES
W H E R E A S  disputes exist between the carriers represented by the 
N ational R ailw ay L abor C onference, designated in L ist A  attached 
hereto and made a part h ereof, and certain o f  their em ployees repre­
sented by the B rotherhood o f L ocom otive Firem en and Enginem en, a 
labor organ ization ; and
W H E R E A S  these disputes have not h eretofore been adjusted under 
the provisions o f  the R ailw ay L abor A ct, as am ended; and
W H E R E A S  these disputes, in the judgm ent o f the N ational M edi­
ation B oard, threaten substantially to interrupt interstate com m erce 
to a degree such as to deprive the country o f essential transportation 
service:
N O W , T H E R E F O R E , by virtue o f the authority vested in me by 
Section 10 o f  the R ailw ay L abor A ct,' as amended (45 U .S.C . 160), I  
hereby create a board, to be appointed by me, to investigate these 
disputes. N o member o f the board shall be pecuniarily or otherwise 
interested in any organization o f railroad em ployees o r any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President w ith respect to 
the disputes w ithin th irty days from  the date o f this order.
A s provided by Section 10 o f the R ailw ay L abor A ct, as amended, 
from  this date and fo r  th irty days after the board has made its report 
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made b y the 
carriers represented by the N ational R ailw ay L abor C onference, or by 
their em ployees, in  the conditions out o f w hich the disputes arose.

research_rationale:
EO 11180 (1964-09-24, 29 FR 13365) creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate disputes between the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Firemen and Enginemen, directs the board to report within thirty days, and recites the statutory standstill that section 10 imposes on the parties from the order's date until thirty days after the report. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11180.txt, 29 FR 13365, PDF pages 7-9) and confirmed that its printed number, title and signature date match the census register row. The order has one operative paragraph with no numbered sections and no stated end date, so the dossier's single whole-order clause is the complete inventory (any carrier list the order attaches is an incorporated list, not a separate command). EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt) revokes the order by number in its table. The first end is that express revocation. The report deadline, the report itself and the end of the standstill are not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, and no held reviewed source establishes the dates on which the board reported or the standstill ran out. Bounded search read for this order: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09; eCFR and GovInfo CFR bulk through 2026-10-14; Federal Register catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts), after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning; the Cruden by-number scan of held order texts in the packet's LOOKUPS.md; and a full read of EO 12553 (held FR text, 33,227 characters).
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Own terms: the order states a report deadline (thirty days) and a standstill running (thirty days after the report). A report deadline is a deadline, not an end, and the standstill is a spent fact whose date no held source fixes; neither is recorded as an end. The order states no date on which it ends. Held later instruments: the by-number scan lists no held later order that cites this order other than EO 12553, which names it in its revocation table; the Federal Register catalog note records the EO 12553 revocation and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches return no hit. No unnamed statute or order was found that would be an earlier candidate end beyond section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, the statute the order itself invokes.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order (1) creates the board and bars members with a financial or organizational interest, (2) directs a report within thirty days and (3) recites the section 10 standstill. Command (3) rests on the statute, which binds the parties for its own thirty-day period regardless of the order, so it is not an independent surviving command of the order. The order makes no appointment by name, creates no fund or property right and delegates no continuing authority, so nothing in it outlives its revocation.","savings_check":"Savings: no savings language in EO 12553 or in this order; the completed facts are spent and nothing continues independently.","scope_check":"Whole-order scope: EO 12553 revokes the order in full. Its table lists the order by number with no 'in part' or section limitation, so the single clause ends on the revocation date, and the held sources record no partial amendment of this order."}

savings_residuals.reason: EO 12553 has no savings, exception, pending-matter or 'nothing herein' wording (searched in the full held text). Its revocation therefore leaves nothing of this order in operation. The creation of the board, any report and the statutory standstill are completed facts, not continuing commands; their dates are not established by a held reviewed source, so no earlier end is claimed. The order created no continuing right, fund or appointment.

first_end.mechanism: express revocation by EO 12553: its operative sentence ends with the words "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and is followed by a two-column table headed 'No. Subject' whose entry "11206 Providing for inspection of interest equalization tax returns" names this order by number; EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording (the full held text was searched for effective, take effect, except, provided, saving, nothing and pending), so the revocation is read as taking effect on signing, February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986; filed February 26, 1986). The signing-date reading is an inference from the order's heading and signature block, not express wording.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: The order directs that returns made in respect of the tax imposed by chapter 41 of the Internal Revenue Code shall be open to inspection by certain classes of persons and government establishments under the Treasury rules it names, and says it is effective on filing for publication. It ended with the whole order: first end EO 12553, 1986-02-25, which revokes the order by number ("11206 Providing for inspection of interest equalization tax returns"). The order has no end date of its own. Earlier candidate ends that do not name this order, disclosed under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on unnamed instruments (option C; none is the end because none names EO 11206): (1) Pub. L. 93-17, section 2 (Apr. 10, 1973), amended section 4911(d) of the Internal Revenue Code to read 'June 30,1974' in place of 'March 31, 1973' (held at jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_11206_Tax_Reform_Act_of_1976_Pub._L._94-455_sec._1202_90_Stat._1667_same_request_as_for_EO__e9de5b9dcd.txt, 87 Stat. 12); (2) the Tax Reform Act of 1976, Pub. L. 94-455 (Oct. 4, 1976), which repealed chapter 41 (interest equalization tax) with the repeal applying to acquisitions made after June 30, 1974, and rewrote section 6103 effective January 1, 1977 under section 1202(i) (held at jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_11206_Tax_Reform_Act_of_1976_Pub._L._94-455_sec._1202_90_Stat._1667_same_request_as_for_EO__1a89ddecb7.txt, 90 Stat. 1520, 1667-1668). The order rests on section 6103(a) as amended by the Interest Equalization Tax Act; I did not establish that either enactment extinguished this order's command, and the 26 U.S.C. 6103 note in the U.S. Code release point records that this order was revoked by EO 12553.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
By virtue of the authority vested in me by section 6103(a) of the  
Internal Revenue Code of 1954 (68A Stat. 753; 26 U.S.C. 6103(a )),  
as amended by section 3(c) of the Interest Equalization Tax Act  
(78 Stat. 844), it is hereby ordered that returns made in respect of  
the tax imposed by chapter 41 of such Code shall be open to inspec­
tion by certain classes of persons and State and Federal government  
establishments in accordance and upon compliance with the rules and  
regulations prescribed by the Secretary of the Treasury in Treasury  
Decision 6543, relating tor inspection and use of returns by such classes  
of persons and State and Federal government establishments, ap­
proved by the President on January 17,1961, the amendment thereto  
approved by the President on April 4, 1963, and the amendment  
thereto approved by me this date.
This order shall be effective upon its filing for publication in the  
F ederal  R egister .
L tndon  B. J ohnson

Tuesday, March 23, 1965 FEDERAL REGISTER 3741
Executive Order 11206
INSPECTION OF INTEREST EQUALIZATION TAX RETURNS
By virtue of the authority vested in me by section 6103(a) of the  
Internal Revenue Code of 1954 (68A Stat. 753; 26 U.S.C. 6103(a )),  
as amended by section 3(c) of the Interest Equalization Tax Act  
(78 Stat. 844), it is hereby ordered that returns made in respect of  
the tax imposed by chapter 41 of such Code shall be open to inspec­
tion by certain classes of persons and State and Federal government  
establishments in accordance and upon compliance with the rules and  
regulations prescribed by the Secretary of the Treasury in Treasury  
Decision 6543, relating tor inspection and use of returns by such classes  
of persons and State and Federal government establishments, ap­
proved by the President on January 17,1961, the amendment thereto  
approved by the President on April 4, 1963, and the amendment  
thereto approved by me this date.
This order shall be effective upon its filing for publication in the  
F ederal  R egister .

research_rationale:
EO 11206 (1965-03-18, 30 FR 3741) is an order under section 6103(a) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1954, as amended by section 3(c) of the Interest Equalization Tax Act, opening certain interest equalization tax returns to inspection. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11206.txt, 30 FR 3741, PDF pages 7-7) and confirmed its number, title and signature date against the census register. EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25) revokes it by number; the dossier already carries the agent-located, independently upheld ACT record for that revocation, which I checked against the held EO 12553 text (operative sentence and table row "11206 Providing for inspection of interest equalization tax returns"). The first end is that express revocation. Earlier candidate ends that do not name this order, disclosed under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on unnamed instruments (option C; none is the end because none names EO 11206): (1) Pub. L. 93-17, section 2 (Apr. 10, 1973), amended section 4911(d) of the Internal Revenue Code to read 'June 30,1974' in place of 'March 31, 1973' (held at jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_11206_Tax_Reform_Act_of_1976_Pub._L._94-455_sec._1202_90_Stat._1667_same_request_as_for_EO__e9de5b9dcd.txt, 87 Stat. 12); (2) the Tax Reform Act of 1976, Pub. L. 94-455 (Oct. 4, 1976), which repealed chapter 41 (interest equalization tax) with the repeal applying to acquisitions made after June 30, 1974, and rewrote section 6103 effective January 1, 1977 under section 1202(i) (held at jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_11206_Tax_Reform_Act_of_1976_Pub._L._94-455_sec._1202_90_Stat._1667_same_request_as_for_EO__1a89ddecb7.txt, 90 Stat. 1520, 1667-1668). The order rests on section 6103(a) as amended by the Interest Equalization Tax Act; I did not establish that either enactment extinguished this order's command, and the 26 U.S.C. 6103 note in the U.S. Code release point records that this order was revoked by EO 12553. Bounded search read for this order: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09; eCFR and GovInfo CFR bulk through 2026-10-14; Federal Register catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts), after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning; the Cruden by-number scan of held order texts in the packet's LOOKUPS.md; and a full read of EO 12553 (held FR text, 33,227 characters).

By virtue of the authority vested in me by section 6103(a) of the 
Internal Revenue Code of 1954 (68A Stat. 753; 26 U.S.C. 6103(a)), 
as amended by section 3(c) of the Interest Equalization Tax Act

and regulations prescribed by the Secretary of the Treasury in a 
Treasury decision, relating to inspection of certain interest equaliza­
tion tax information returns by the Board of Governors of the Federal 
Reserve System and the Federal Reserve Banks, approved by me this 
date.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: The order's single operative text creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate a dispute between the Atchison, Topeka and Santa Fe Railway Company, Lines East and West, and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, directs it to report within thirty days, and recites the statutory standstill for thirty days after the report. It ended with the whole order: first end EO 12553, 1986-02-25, which revokes the order by number ("11243 Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute"). The report deadline is a deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines), and the end of the standstill is a spent fact whose date no held reviewed source fixes, so neither is recorded as an earlier end or as a later event. The order states no end date of its own, and no held instrument other than EO 12553 names it.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Executive Order 11243
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE DISPUTE BETWEEN
THE ATCHISON, TOPEKA AND SANTA FE RAILWAY COMPANY, LINES
EAST AND WEST, AND CERTAIN OF THEIR EMPLOYEES
W H E R E A S  a dispute exists between the Atchison, Topeka and 
Santa Fe Railway Company, Lines East and West, and certain of their 
employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, a 
labor organization; and
W H E R E A S  this dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under the 
provisions^ the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
, W H E R E A S  this dispute, in the judgment of the National Media­
tion Board, threatens substantially to interrupt interstate commerce 
to a degree such as to deprive a section of the country of essential 
transportation service:
N O W , T H E R E F O R E , by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
Section 10 o f the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), 
I  hereby create a board of three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate this dispute..  N o member of the board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or 
any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to 
the dispute within thirty days from the date o f this order.
As provided by Section 10 o f the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report 
to the President, no .change, except by agreement, shall be made by 
the carrier or by their employees, in the conditions out o f which the 
dispute arose.

research_rationale:
EO 11243 (1965-09-11, 30 FR 11709) creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate a dispute between the Atchison, Topeka and Santa Fe Railway Company, Lines East and West, and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, directs the board to report within thirty days, and recites the statutory standstill that section 10 imposes on the parties from the order's date until thirty days after the report. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11243.txt, 30 FR 11709, PDF pages 5-5) and confirmed that its printed number, title and signature date match the census register row. The order has one operative paragraph with no numbered sections and no stated end date, so the dossier's single whole-order clause is the complete inventory (any carrier list the order attaches is an incorporated list, not a separate command). EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt) revokes the order by number in its table. The first end is that express revocation. The report deadline, the report itself and the end of the standstill are not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, and no held reviewed source establishes the dates on which the board reported or the standstill ran out. Bounded search read for this order: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09; eCFR and GovInfo CFR bulk through 2026-10-14; Federal Register catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts), after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning; the Cruden by-number scan of held order texts in the packet's LOOKUPS.md; and a full read of EO 12553 (held FR text, 33,227 characters).

A report deadline is a deadline, not an end, and the standstill is a spent fact whose date no held source fixes; neither is recorded as an end. The order states no date on which it ends. Held later instruments: the by-number scan lists no held later order that cites this order other than EO 12553, which names it in its revocation table; the Federal Register catalog note records the EO 12553 revocation and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches return no hit. No unnamed statute or order was found that would be an earlier candidate end beyond section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, the statute the order itself invokes.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order (1) creates the board and bars members with a financial or organizational interest, (2) directs a report within thirty days and (3) recites the section 10 standstill. Command (3) rests on the statute, which binds the parties for its own thirty-day period regardless of the order, so it is not an independent surviving command of the order. The order makes no appointment by name, creates no fund or property right and delegates no continuing authority, so nothing in it outlives its revocation.","savings_check":"Savings: no savings language in EO 12553 or in this order; the completed facts are spent and nothing continues independently.","scope_check":"Whole-order scope: EO 12553 revokes the order in full. Its table lists the order by number with no 'in part' or section limitation, so the single clause ends on the revocation date, and the held sources record no partial amendment of this order."}

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: The order's single operative text creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate disputes between the air carriers represented by the Five Carriers Negotiating Committee and certain of their employees represented by the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers, directs it to report within thirty days, and recites the statutory standstill for thirty days after the report. It ended with the whole order: first end EO 12553, 1986-02-25, which revokes the order by number ("11276 Creating an emergency board to investigate an airline labor dispute"). The report deadline is a deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines), and the end of the standstill is a spent fact whose date no held reviewed source fixes, so neither is recorded as an earlier end or as a later event. The order states no end date of its own, and no held instrument other than EO 12553 names it.

Presidential Documents
Title 3— THE PRESIDENT
Executive O rder 11276
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE DISPUTES BE­
TWEEN THE CARRIERS REPRESENTED BY THE FIVE CARRIERS NEGO­
TIATING COMMITTEE AND CERTAIN OF THEIR EMPLOYEES
W H E R E A S disputes exist between the air carriers represented by 
the Five Carriers Negotiating Committee, designated in List A, at­
tached hereto and made a part hereof, and certain of their employees 
represented by the International Association of Machinists and Aero­
space Workers, A FL -C IO , a labor organization; and
W H E R E A S these disputes have not heretofore been adjusted under 
the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
W H E R E A S these disputes, in the judgment of the National Media­
tion Board, threaten substantially to interrupt interstate commerce 
to a degree such as to deprive the country of essential transportation 
service:
NOW, T H E R E F O R E , by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), I  
hereby create a board of three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate these disputes. No member of the board shall be pecuni­
arily or otherwise interested in any organization of airline employees 
or in any air carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect 
to the disputes within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report 
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by 
the carriers represented by the Five Carriers Negotiating Committee, 
or by their employees, in the conditions out of which the disputes arose.

W H E R E A S these disputes have not heretofore been adjusted under 
the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
W H E R E A S these disputes, in the judgment of the National Media­
tion Board, threaten substantially to interrupt interstate commerce 
to a degree such as to deprive the country of essential transportation 
service:
NOW, T H E R E F O R E , by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), I  
hereby create a board of three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate these disputes. No member of the board shall be pecuni­
arily or otherwise interested in any organization of airline employees 
or in any air carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect 
to the disputes within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report 
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by 
the carriers represented by the Five Carriers Negotiating Committee, 
or by their employees, in the conditions out of which the disputes arose.

research_rationale:
EO 11276 (1966-04-21, 31 FR 6233) creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate disputes between the air carriers represented by the Five Carriers Negotiating Committee and certain of their employees represented by the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers, directs the board to report within thirty days, and recites the statutory standstill that section 10 imposes on the parties from the order's date until thirty days after the report. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11276.txt, 31 FR 6233, PDF pages 5-5) and confirmed that its printed number, title and signature date match the census register row. The order has one operative paragraph with no numbered sections and no stated end date, so the dossier's single whole-order clause is the complete inventory (any carrier list the order attaches is an incorporated list, not a separate command). EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt) revokes the order by number in its table. The first end is that express revocation. The report deadline, the report itself and the end of the standstill are not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, and no held reviewed source establishes the dates on which the board reported or the standstill ran out. Bounded search read for this order: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09; eCFR and GovInfo CFR bulk through 2026-10-14; Federal Register catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts), after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning; the Cruden by-number scan of held order texts in the packet's LOOKUPS.md; and a full read of EO 12553 (held FR text, 33,227 characters).
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Own terms: the order states a report deadline (\"within thirty days from the date of this order\") and a standstill running (\"for thirty days after the board has made its report\"). A report deadline is a deadline, not an end, and the standstill is a spent fact whose date no held source fixes; neither is recorded as an end. The order states no date on which it ends. Held later instruments: the by-number scan lists no held later order that cites this order other than EO 12553, which names it in its revocation table; the Federal Register catalog note records the EO 12553 revocation and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches return no hit. No unnamed statute or order was found that would be an earlier candidate end beyond section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, the statute the order itself invokes.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order (1) creates the board and bars members with a financial or organizational interest, (2) directs a report within thirty days and (3) recites the section 10 standstill. Command (3) rests on the statute, which binds the parties for its own thirty-day period regardless of the order, so it is not an independent surviving command of the order. The order makes no appointment by name, creates no fund or property right and delegates no continuing authority, so nothing in it outlives its revocation.","savings_check":"Savings: no savings language in EO 12553 or in this order; the completed facts are spent and nothing continues independently.","scope_check":"Whole-order scope: EO 12553 revokes the order in full. Its table lists the order by number with no 'in part' or section limitation, so the single clause ends on the revocation date, and the held sources record no partial amendment of this order."}

savings_residuals.reason: EO 12553 has no savings, exception, pending-matter or 'nothing herein' wording (searched in the full held text). Its revocation therefore leaves nothing of this order in operation. The creation of the board, any report and the statutory standstill are completed facts, not continuing commands; their dates are not established by a held reviewed source, so no earlier end is claimed. The order created no continuing right, fund or appointment.

operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Executive Order 11291
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE A DISPUTE
BETWEEN THE AMERICAN AIRLINES, INC., AND CERTAIN OF ITS
EMPLOYEES
W HEREAS a dispute exists between the American Airlines, Inc., a  
carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Transport  
Workers Union of America, AFL-CIO, a labor organization; and
W HEREAS this dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under  
the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended;  and
W HEREAS this dispute, in the judgment of the National Media­
tion Board, threatens substantially to interrupt interstate commerce to  
a degree such as to deprive, a section of the country of essential  
transportation service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by  
Sections 10 and 201 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C.  
160 and 181, respectively), I hereby create a board of three members, 
to be appointed by me, to investigate this dispute. No member of the  
board shall be pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization  
of airline employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to  
this dispute within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended,  
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report  
to the President, no change, except by agreement', shall be made by the  
American Airlines, Inc., or by its employees, in the conditions out of  
which this dispute arose.

research_rationale:
EO 11291 (1966-07-27, 31 FR 10175) creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate a dispute between American Airlines, Inc., and certain of its employees represented by the Transport Workers Union of America (sections 10 and 201 of the Railway Labor Act), directs the board to report within thirty days, and recites the statutory standstill that section 10 imposes on the parties from the order's date until thirty days after the report. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11291.txt, 31 FR 10175, PDF pages 5-5) and confirmed that its printed number, title and signature date match the census register row. The order has one operative paragraph with no numbered sections and no stated end date, so the dossier's single whole-order clause is the complete inventory (any carrier list the order attaches is an incorporated list, not a separate command). EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt) revokes the order by number in its table. The first end is that express revocation. The report deadline, the report itself and the end of the standstill are not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, and no held reviewed source establishes the dates on which the board reported or the standstill ran out. Bounded search read for this order: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09; eCFR and GovInfo CFR bulk through 2026-10-14; Federal Register catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts), after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning; the Cruden by-number scan of held order texts in the packet's LOOKUPS.md; and a full read of EO 12553 (held FR text, 33,227 characters).

A report deadline is a deadline, not an end, and the standstill is a spent fact whose date no held source fixes; neither is recorded as an end. The order states no date on which it ends. Held later instruments: the by-number scan lists no held later order that cites this order other than EO 12553, which names it in its revocation table; the Federal Register catalog note records the EO 12553 revocation and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches return no hit. No unnamed statute or order was found that would be an earlier candidate end beyond section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, the statute the order itself invokes.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order (1) creates the board and bars members with a financial or organizational interest, (2) directs a report within thirty days and (3) recites the section 10 standstill. Command (3) rests on the statute, which binds the parties for its own thirty-day period regardless of the order, so it is not an independent surviving command of the order. The order makes no appointment by name, creates no fund or property right and delegates no continuing authority, so nothing in it outlives its revocation.","savings_check":"Savings: no savings language in EO 12553 or in this order; the completed facts are spent and nothing continues independently.","scope_check":"Whole-order scope: EO 12553 revokes the order in full. Its table lists the order by number with no 'in part' or section limitation, so the single clause ends on the revocation date, and the held sources record no partial amendment of this order."}

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: The order waives, for one named employee, the limit in section 1 of EO 9721 on the period treated as leave of absence and deems him on leave from March 9, 1954 through September 12, 1957 for the purposes of EO 9721. It ended with the whole order: first end EO 12553, 1986-02-25, which revokes it by number ("11303 Modifying provisions for transfer of personnel to certain public international organizations"). The waiver took effect on the order's own date (1966-09-12), a disclosed alternative reading of exhaustion that is not adopted as the end because the deeming operates for the rights and benefits provided by EO 9721, which remained in force until the same revocation. The surviving consequence is recorded under savings.

By virtue of the authority vested in me by the Civil Service Act 
(22 Stat. 403) and Section 1753 of the Revised Statutes, and as Presi­

of May 10, 1946, as amended by Executive Order No. 10103 of 
February 1, 1950, providing for the transfer of personnel to public 
international organizations in which the United States Government 
participates be, and it is hereby, modified as follows:
The limitation in Section 1 relating to the period during which an 
employee shall be considered as on leave of absence from his employ­
ment with the Federal Government is waived with respect to Reginald 
C. Price, and he shall be considered to have been on leave of absence for 
the period March 9,1954, through September 12,1957, for the purpose 
of all rights and benefits provided by Executive Order No. 9721, as 
amended.

research_rationale:
EO 11303 (1966-09-12, 31 FR 11963) modifies EO 9721, as amended by EO 10103, by waiving for Reginald C. Price the limitation in section 1 on the period during which an employee is considered on leave of absence, and deeming him on leave from March 9, 1954 through September 12, 1957 for the purpose of all rights and benefits under EO 9721. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11303.txt, 31 FR 11963, PDF pages 5-5) and confirmed its number, title and date against the census register. The order is a single paragraph with one operative command, so the dossier's single clause is the complete inventory. EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25) revokes EO 11303 by number (row "11303 Modifying provisions for transfer of personnel to certain public international organizations") and also lists EO 9721. The first end is that express revocation. The waiver is a one-person act that took effect on the order's date; under the owner ruling of 2026-10-28 the exhausted waiver is distinguished from the surviving consequence (the credited leave period and the rights that rest on it), and no held source shows an earlier cessation of the command. The alternative reading, that the self-executing deeming was exhausted when the order took effect on 1966-09-12, is disclosed for the reviewer; I did not adopt it because the deeming operates 'for the purpose of all rights and benefits provided by' EO 9721, which stayed in force until EO 12553 revoked it. Bounded search read for this order: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09; eCFR and GovInfo CFR bulk through 2026-10-14; Federal Register catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts), after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning; the Cruden by-number scan of held order texts in the packet's LOOKUPS.md; and a full read of EO 12553 (held FR text, 33,227 characters).

That period is the subject of the deeming, not a term of the command. No held later order other than EO 12553 names EO 11303; EO 12553 also lists the amended EO 9721, so the parent order ended the same day. The dossier's missing item for EO 10103 concerns an earlier amendment of the parent order, not an event after this order. Disclosed alternative end (not adopted): 1966-09-12, the order's own date, if the self-executing waiver is treated as exhausted when it took effect.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order contains only the waiver and deeming for one named person; it creates no appointment, fund or delegation. The surviving consequence is the person's credited leave status and the benefits resting on it, which the order recorded rather than continued as a command.","savings_check":"Savings: no savings language in EO 12553; the credited leave status and accrued benefits are surviving consequences, separate from the exhausted waiver command.","scope_check":"Whole-order scope: EO 12553 revokes the order in full, with no 'in part' limitation in its table entry."}

savings_residuals.reason: EO 12553 has no savings, exception, pending-matter or 'nothing herein' wording (searched in the full held text), so the revocation does not preserve the order as a command. The credited leave period for the named employee and any rights and benefits that accrued under EO 9721 while it was in force are accrued consequences; the held sources do not show any open claim.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: The order's single operative text creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate a dispute between Pan American World Airways, Inc., and certain of its employees represented by the Transport Workers Union of America (sections 10 and 201 of the Railway Labor Act), directs it to report within thirty days, and recites the statutory standstill for thirty days after the report. It ended with the whole order: first end EO 12553, 1986-02-25, which revokes the order by number ("11308 Creating an emergency board to investigate an airline labor dispute"). The report deadline is a deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines), and the end of the standstill is a spent fact whose date no held reviewed source fixes, so neither is recorded as an earlier end or as a later event. The order states no end date of its own, and no held instrument other than EO 12553 names it.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Executive Order 11308
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE A DISPUTE BE­
TWEEN THE PAN AMERICAN WORLD AIRWAYS, INC., AND CERTAIN
OF ITS EMPLOYEES
W H E R E AS a dispute exists between the Pan American World 
Airways, Inc., a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by 
the Transport Workers Union of America, A F L-C IO , a labor orga­
nization ; and
W H E R E AS this dispute has not heretofore been adjusted under the 
provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
W H E R E AS this dispute, in the judgment of the National Media­
tion Board, threatens substantially to interrupt interstate commerce to 
a degree such as to deprive a section of the country of essential trans­
portation service:
NOW, TH EREFO RE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
Sections 10 and 201 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45U.S.C. 
160 and 181, respectively) ^  I  hereby create a board of three members, 
to be appointed by me, to investigate.this dispute. No member of the 
board shall be pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization 
of airline employees or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to 
this dispute within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report 
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the 
Pan American World Airways, Inc., or by its employees, in the con­
ditions out of which this dispute arose.

research_rationale:
EO 11308 (1966-09-30, 31 FR 12919) creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate a dispute between Pan American World Airways, Inc., and certain of its employees represented by the Transport Workers Union of America (sections 10 and 201 of the Railway Labor Act), directs the board to report within thirty days, and recites the statutory standstill that section 10 imposes on the parties from the order's date until thirty days after the report. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11308.txt, 31 FR 12919, PDF pages 7-7) and confirmed that its printed number, title and signature date match the census register row. The order has one operative paragraph with no numbered sections and no stated end date, so the dossier's single whole-order clause is the complete inventory (any carrier list the order attaches is an incorporated list, not a separate command). EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt) revokes the order by number in its table. The first end is that express revocation. The report deadline, the report itself and the end of the standstill are not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, and no held reviewed source establishes the dates on which the board reported or the standstill ran out. Bounded search read for this order: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09; eCFR and GovInfo CFR bulk through 2026-10-14; Federal Register catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts), after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning; the Cruden by-number scan of held order texts in the packet's LOOKUPS.md; and a full read of EO 12553 (held FR text, 33,227 characters).
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Own terms: the order states a report deadline (\"within thirty days from the date of this order\") and a standstill running (\"for thirty days after the board has made its report\"). A report deadline is a deadline, not an end, and the standstill is a spent fact whose date no held source fixes; neither is recorded as an end. The order states no date on which it ends. Held later instruments: the by-number scan lists no held later order that cites this order other than EO 12553, which names it in its revocation table; the Federal Register catalog note records the EO 12553 revocation and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches return no hit. No unnamed statute or order was found that would be an earlier candidate end beyond section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, the statute the order itself invokes.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order (1) creates the board and bars members with a financial or organizational interest, (2) directs a report within thirty days and (3) recites the section 10 standstill. Command (3) rests on the statute, which binds the parties for its own thirty-day period regardless of the order, so it is not an independent surviving command of the order. The order makes no appointment by name, creates no fund or property right and delegates no continuing authority, so nothing in it outlives its revocation.","savings_check":"Savings: no savings language in EO 12553 or in this order; the completed facts are spent and nothing continues independently.","scope_check":"Whole-order scope: EO 12553 revokes the order in full. Its table lists the order by number with no 'in part' or section limitation, so the single clause ends on the revocation date, and the held sources record no partial amendment of this order."}

Its revocation therefore leaves nothing of this order in operation. The creation of the board, any report and the statutory standstill are completed facts, not continuing commands; their dates are not established by a held reviewed source, so no earlier end is claimed. The order created no continuing right, fund or appointment.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: The order's single operative text creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate disputes between the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and certain of their employees represented by the Order of Railway Conductors and Brakemen, directs it to report within thirty days, and recites the statutory standstill for thirty days after the report. It ended with the whole order: first end EO 12553, 1986-02-25, which revokes the order by number ("11356 Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute"). The report deadline is a deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines), and the end of the standstill is a spent fact whose date no held reviewed source fixes, so neither is recorded as an earlier end or as a later event. The order states no end date of its own, and no held instrument other than EO 12553 names it.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Executive Order 11356
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE DISPUTES BE­
TWEEN THE CARRIERS REPRESENTED BY THE NATIONAL RAILWAY
LABOR CONFERENCE AND CERTAIN OF THEIR EMPLOYEES
W HEREAS disputes exist between the carriers represented by the 
National Railway Labor Conference, designated in List A attached 
hereto and made a part hereof, and certain of their employees repre­
sented by the Order of Railway Conductors and Brakemen, a labor 
organization; and
W HEREAS these disputes have not heretofore been adjusted under 
the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended ; and
W HEREAS these disputes, in the judgment of the National Media­
tion Board, threaten substantially to interrupt interstate commerce 
to a degree such as to deprive the country of essential transportation 
service :
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), I 
hereby create a board oi three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate these disputes. No member of the board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or 
any carrier.
The Board shall report its findings to the President with respect to 
the disputes within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report 
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the 
carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference, or 
by their employees, in the conditions out of which the disputes arose.

research_rationale:
EO 11356 (1967-05-30, 32 FR 8019) creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate disputes between the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and certain of their employees represented by the Order of Railway Conductors and Brakemen, directs the board to report within thirty days, and recites the statutory standstill that section 10 imposes on the parties from the order's date until thirty days after the report. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11356.txt, 32 FR 8019, PDF pages 7-8) and confirmed that its printed number, title and signature date match the census register row. The order has one operative paragraph with no numbered sections and no stated end date, so the dossier's single whole-order clause is the complete inventory (any carrier list the order attaches is an incorporated list, not a separate command). EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt) revokes the order by number in its table. The first end is that express revocation. The report deadline, the report itself and the end of the standstill are not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, and no held reviewed source establishes the dates on which the board reported or the standstill ran out. Bounded search read for this order: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09; eCFR and GovInfo CFR bulk through 2026-10-14; Federal Register catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts), after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning; the Cruden by-number scan of held order texts in the packet's LOOKUPS.md; and a full read of EO 12553 (held FR text, 33,227 characters).

A report deadline is a deadline, not an end, and the standstill is a spent fact whose date no held source fixes; neither is recorded as an end. The order states no date on which it ends. Held later instruments: the by-number scan lists no held later order that cites this order other than EO 12553, which names it in its revocation table; the Federal Register catalog note records the EO 12553 revocation and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches return no hit. No unnamed statute or order was found that would be an earlier candidate end beyond section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, the statute the order itself invokes.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order (1) creates the board and bars members with a financial or organizational interest, (2) directs a report within thirty days and (3) recites the section 10 standstill. Command (3) rests on the statute, which binds the parties for its own thirty-day period regardless of the order, so it is not an independent surviving command of the order. The order makes no appointment by name, creates no fund or property right and delegates no continuing authority, so nothing in it outlives its revocation.","savings_check":"Savings: no savings language in EO 12553 or in this order; the completed facts are spent and nothing continues independently.","scope_check":"Whole-order scope: EO 12553 revokes the order in full. Its table lists the order by number with no 'in part' or section limitation, so the single clause ends on the revocation date, and the held sources record no partial amendment of this order."}

The order created no continuing right, fund or appointment.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: The order's single operative text creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate disputes between the Illinois Central Railroad Company, the Louisville & Nashville Railroad Company and the Belt Railway Company of Chicago and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, directs it to report within thirty days, and recites the statutory standstill for thirty days after the report. It ended with the whole order: first end EO 12553, 1986-02-25, which revokes the order by number ("11433 Creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute"). The report deadline is a deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines), and the end of the standstill is a spent fact whose date no held reviewed source fixes, so neither is recorded as an earlier end or as a later event. The order states no end date of its own, and no held instrument other than EO 12553 names it.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Executive Order 11433
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE DISPUTES BE­
TWEEN THE ILLINOIS CENTRAL RAILROAD COMPANY, LOUISVILLE &
NASHVILLE RAILROAD COMPANY, AND THE BELT RAILWAY COM­
PANY OF CHICAGO, AND CERTAIN OF THEIR EMPLOYEES
W H E R E A S disputes exist between the Illinois Central Railroad 
Company, Louisville & Nashville Railroad Company, and the Belt 
Railway Company of Chicago, carriers, and certain of their employees 
represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, a labor organi­
zation ; and
W H E R E A S these disputes have not heretofore been adjusted under 
the provisions o f the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
W H E R E A S these disputes, in the judgment of the National Media­
tion Board, threaten substantially to interrupt interstate commerce 
to a degree such as to deprive a section of the country of essential 
transportation service:
N OW  T H E R E FO R E , by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), I 
hereby create a Board of three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate these disputes. No member o f the Board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or 
any carrier.
The Board shall report its findings to the President with respect to 
these disputes within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the Board has made its report 
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the 
Illinois Central Railroad Company, Louisville and Nashville Railroad 
Company, and the Belt Railway Company of Chicago, or by their 
employees, in the conditions out of which these disputes arose.

research_rationale:
EO 11433 (1968-11-06, 33 FR 16379) creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate disputes between the Illinois Central Railroad Company, the Louisville & Nashville Railroad Company and the Belt Railway Company of Chicago and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, directs the board to report within thirty days, and recites the statutory standstill that section 10 imposes on the parties from the order's date until thirty days after the report. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11433.txt, 33 FR 16379, PDF pages 5-5) and confirmed that its printed number, title and signature date match the census register row. The order has one operative paragraph with no numbered sections and no stated end date, so the dossier's single whole-order clause is the complete inventory (any carrier list the order attaches is an incorporated list, not a separate command). EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt) revokes the order by number in its table. The first end is that express revocation. first_end.mechanism: express revocation by EO 12553: its operative sentence ends with the words "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and is followed by a two-column table headed 'No. Subject' whose entry "11444 Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes" names this order by number; EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording (the full held text was searched for effective, take effect, except, provided, saving, nothing and pending), so the revocation is read as taking effect on signing, February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986; filed February 26, 1986). The signing-date reading is an inference from the order's heading and signature block, not express wording.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: The order's single operative text creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate disputes between the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers, directs it to report within thirty days, and recites the statutory standstill for thirty days after the report. It ended with the whole order: first end EO 12553, 1986-02-25, which revokes the order by number ("11444 Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes"). The report deadline is a deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines), and the end of the standstill is a spent fact whose date no held reviewed source fixes, so neither is recorded as an earlier end or as a later event. The order states no end date of its own, and no held instrument other than EO 12553 names it.
operative_clauses.original_operative_text:
Executive Order 11444
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE DISPUTES BE­
TWEEN THE CARRIERS REPRESENTED BY THE NATIONAL RAILWAY
LABOR CONFERENCE AND CERTAIN OF THEIR EMPLOYEES
WHEREAS disputes exist between the carriers represented by the 
National Railway Labor Conference, designated in List A attached 
hereto and made a part hereof, and certain of their employees repre­
sented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers, a labor organi­
zation ; and
WHEREAS these disputes have not heretofore Keen adjusted under 
the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended; and
WHEREAS these disputes, in the judgment of the National Media­
tion Board, threaten substantially to interrupt interstate commerce to 
a degree such as to deprive the country of essential transportation

NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by

National Railway Labor Conference, designated in List A attached

zation ; and

service:

hereby create a board of three members, to be appointed by me, to in­
vestigate these disputes. No member of the board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees 
or any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to 
the disputes within thirty days from the date of this order.
As provided by Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report 
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by

research_rationale:
EO 11444 (1969-01-13, 34 FR 543) creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate disputes between the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers, directs the board to report within thirty days, and recites the statutory standstill that section 10 imposes on the parties from the order's date until thirty days after the report. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11444.txt, 34 FR 543, PDF pages 7-8) and confirmed that its printed number, title and signature date match the census register row. The order has one operative paragraph with no numbered sections and no stated end date, so the dossier's single whole-order clause is the complete inventory (any carrier list the order attaches is an incorporated list, not a separate command). EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt) revokes the order by number in its table. The first end is that express revocation. The report deadline, the report itself and the end of the standstill are not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, and no held reviewed source establishes the dates on which the board reported or the standstill ran out. Bounded search read for this order: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09; eCFR and GovInfo CFR bulk through 2026-10-14; Federal Register catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts), after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning; the Cruden by-number scan of held order texts in the packet's LOOKUPS.md; and a full read of EO 12553 (held FR text, 33,227 characters).
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Own terms: the order states a report deadline (\"within thirty days from the date of this order\") and a standstill running (\"for thirty days after the board has made its report\"). A report deadline is a deadline, not an end, and the standstill is a spent fact whose date no held source fixes; neither is recorded as an end. The order states no date on which it ends. Held later instruments: the by-number scan lists no held later order that cites this order other than EO 12553, which names it in its revocation table; the Federal Register catalog note records the EO 12553 revocation and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches return no hit. No unnamed statute or order was found that would be an earlier candidate end beyond section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, the statute the order itself invokes.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order (1) creates the board and bars members with a financial or organizational interest, (2) directs a report within thirty days and (3) recites the section 10 standstill. Command (3) rests on the statute, which binds the parties for its own thirty-day period regardless of the order, so it is not an independent surviving command of the order. The order makes no appointment by name, creates no fund or property right and delegates no continuing authority, so nothing in it outlives its revocation.","savings_check":"Savings: no savings language in EO 12553 or in this order; the completed facts are spent and nothing continues independently.","scope_check":"Whole-order scope: EO 12553 revokes the order in full. Its table lists the order by number with no 'in part' or section limitation, so the single clause ends on the revocation date, and the held sources record no partial amendment of this order."}

savings_residuals.reason: EO 12553 has no savings, exception, pending-matter or 'nothing herein' wording (searched in the full held text). Its revocation therefore leaves nothing of this order in operation. The creation of the board, any report and the statutory standstill are completed facts, not continuing commands; their dates are not established by a held reviewed source, so no earlier end is claimed. The order created no continuing right, fund or appointment.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: whole: The order's single operative text creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate disputes between the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Signalmen, directs it to report within thirty days, and recites the statutory standstill for thirty days after the report. It ended with the whole order: first end EO 12553, 1986-02-25, which revokes the order by number ("11445 Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes"). The report deadline is a deadline, not an end (owner ruling 2026-10-21 on report deadlines), and the end of the standstill is a spent fact whose date no held reviewed source fixes, so neither is recorded as an earlier end or as a later event. The order states no end date of its own, and no held instrument other than EO 12553 names it.

Executive Order 11445
CREATING AN EMERGENCY BOARD TO INVESTIGATE DISPUTES BE­
TWEEN THE CARRIERS REPRESENTED BY THE NATIONAL RAILWAY
LABOR CONFERENCE AND CERTAIN OF THEIR EMPLOYEES
WHEREAS disputes exist between the carriers represented by the 
National Railway Labor Conference, designated in List A attached 
hereto and made a part hereof, and certain of their employees repre­
sented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Signalmen, a labor organiza­tion ; and
WHEREAS these disputes have not heretofore been adjusted under 
the provisions of the Railway Labor Act, as amended ; and
WHEREAS these disputes, in the judgment of thè National Media­
tion Board, threaten substantially to interrupt interstate commerce to 
a degree such as to deprive the country of essential transportation 
service:
NOW, THEREFORE, by virtue of the authority vested in me by 
Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as aihended (45 TJ.S.C. 160), I 
hereby create à board of three members, to be appointed by me, to 
investigate these disputes. No member of the board shall be pecuniarily 
or otherwise interested in any organization of railroad employees or 
any carrier.
The board shall report its findings to the President with respect to 
the disputes within thirty days from the date of this order.
As prpvided by Section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended, 
from this date and for thirty days after the board has made its report 
to the President, no change, except by agreement, shall be made by the 
carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference, or by 
their employees, in the conditions out of which the disputes arose.

research_rationale:
EO 11445 (1969-01-13, 34 FR 545) creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act to investigate disputes between the carriers represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and certain of their employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Signalmen, directs the board to report within thirty days, and recites the statutory standstill that section 10 imposes on the parties from the order's date until thirty days after the report. I read the full held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11445.txt, 34 FR 545, PDF pages 9-10) and confirmed that its printed number, title and signature date match the census register row. The order has one operative paragraph with no numbered sections and no stated end date, so the dossier's single whole-order clause is the complete inventory (any carrier list the order attaches is an incorporated list, not a separate command). EO 12553 (signed 1986-02-25; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12553.txt) revokes the order by number in its table. The first end is that express revocation. The report deadline, the report itself and the end of the standstill are not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, and no held reviewed source establishes the dates on which the board reported or the standstill ran out. Bounded search read for this order: the dossier's three machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09; eCFR and GovInfo CFR bulk through 2026-10-14; Federal Register catalog disposition notes and operative sentences of 17,521 saved order texts), after reading their coverage notes, which carry no coverage warning; the Cruden by-number scan of held order texts in the packet's LOOKUPS.md; and a full read of EO 12553 (held FR text, 33,227 characters).
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Own terms: the order states a report deadline (\"within thirty days from the date of this order\") and a standstill running (\"for thirty days after the board has made its report\"). A report deadline is a deadline, not an end, and the standstill is a spent fact whose date no held source fixes; neither is recorded as an end. The order states no date on which it ends. Held later instruments: the by-number scan lists no held later order that cites this order other than EO 12553, which names it in its revocation table; the Federal Register catalog note records the EO 12553 revocation and the U.S. Code and eCFR searches return no hit. No unnamed statute or order was found that would be an earlier candidate end beyond section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, the statute the order itself invokes.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: the order (1) creates the board and bars members with a financial or organizational interest, (2) directs a report within thirty days and (3) recites the section 10 standstill. Command (3) rests on the statute, which binds the parties for its own thirty-day period regardless of the order, so it is not an independent surviving command of the order. The order makes no appointment by name, creates no fund or property right and delegates no continuing authority, so nothing in it outlives its revocation.","savings_check":"Savings: no savings language in EO 12553 or in this order; the completed facts are spent and nothing continues independently.","scope_check":"Whole-order scope: EO 12553 revokes the order in full. Its table lists the order by number with no 'in part' or section limitation, so the single clause ends on the revocation date, and the held sources record no partial amendment of this order."}

savings_residuals.reason: EO 12553 has no savings, exception, pending-matter or 'nothing herein' wording (searched in the full held text). Its revocation therefore leaves nothing of this order in operation. The creation of the board, any report and the statutory standstill are completed facts, not continuing commands; their dates are not established by a held reviewed source, so no earlier end is claimed. The order created no continuing right, fund or appointment.

whole_order_end.mechanism: express revocation by EO 12553: its operative sentence ends with the words "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" and is followed by a two-column table headed 'No. Subject' whose entry "11445 Creating an emergency board to investigate railroad labor disputes" names this order by number; EO 12553 contains no effective-date wording (the full held text was searched for effective, take effect, except, provided, saving, nothing and pending), so the revocation is read as taking effect on signing, February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, printed March 3, 1986; filed February 26, 1986). The signing-date reading is an inference from the order's heading and signature block, not express wording.
